rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. I did not request implementation source. The test text was enough to map each obligation to an assertion.

**Resolving a selector from the root against the retained outline**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. It checks that `text()` equals the item's source span and that `structural_hash()` equals the item's hash. It also selects the empty selector for the root.
- The Markdown test `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` selects percent-encoded, `#N`-numbered and anonymous `block@` items.
- `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` selects items numbered with `#N`.
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` selects plain-text lines.

**Returning an owned `OutlineContent` that shares the snapshot and fingerprinting rules**
- The Rust and Markdown tests assert `std::ptr::eq(selected.outline(), contents.outline())`. The Markdown test also calls `select` on an already-selected item (`second.select(main)`), and that succeeds.
- `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` checks three things after the language and scheme objects are dropped:
  - A selected item keeps the `custom-v2` scheme.
  - Selecting from a loaded handle and from a supplied-source handle gives equal fingerprints.
  - A different scheme (`custom-v3`) gives a different fingerprint with the same structural hash.

**No extra file read, and usable after the original handle is dropped**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` drops `file` and rewrites the file on disk. It then checks that `selected` and `selected_again` still report the old text and fingerprint.
- It also calls `selected.select("")` after the edit and gets the original root text `"first\nsecond\n"`. That shows selection used the retained snapshot rather than re-reading the file.
- The same test shows `from_id` fails after the edit, which contrasts with `select`.

**`id()` and `text()` contract, including attached source and text before redaction**
- The Rust test checks that a selected function's `text()` starts with its `///` doc comment and contains `#[inline]`, and that its span starts at the doc comment.
- `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` checks that the selected item's `text()` still contains the token while `format()` is redacted.
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` checks `id()` equality for selected items and for the retained root.

**Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable**
- `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` checks that duplicate `alpha` lines share a selector and that selecting it returns `"alpha"`.
- `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` selects the shared selector of two identical `same` lines and gets `"same"`.
- The same test builds a custom `line`-kind language whose items have different hashes. Selecting that selector returns an "ambiguous" error, so the `line` exemption applies only to identical content.

**Errors for invalid, missing and ambiguous selections**
- `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` asserts that the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing selector `fn[absent]` both return errors.
- The ambiguous case is covered by the custom language with duplicate `part[same]` items (error contains "ambiguous"). The CSS test also asserts that `rule[a%20b]` without `#N` is an error.

Selector syntax and error semantics are cited context. Their own requirements are assessed separately, and the selection tests above still exercise their application here. I found no gap: each obligation has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
